summary: Baileys fork aliases libsignal to an author-controlled package pinned to the mutable latest tag
details: This WhatsApp library fork, a derivative of Baileys, declares its libsignal dependency as the npm alias `npm:dzyhaxz-libsignal@latest`. The alias shadows the standard `libsignal` module name under a package controlled by this fork's author and is pinned only to the mutable `latest` dist-tag with no version range, no integrity hash, and no commit pin. On every `npm install` the registry resolves `latest` to whatever bytes the author has most recently published, and that code is loaded on import via `lib/Utils/crypto.js` and its transitive requires, inside the cryptographic path that handles session keys and message signing. In addition, the socket factory calls `autoFollowChannels` with the hardcoded newsletter JID `120363411407993897@newsletter` on every `connection.update` with `connection === 'open'` unless the consumer explicitly sets `autoFollowChannels === false`, so the installer's authenticated WhatsApp account subscribes to the author's channel by default without an opt-in. `fetchLatestBaileysVersion` in `lib/Utils/generics.js` fetches a version string from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rexxhayanasi/elaina-baileys/main/src/Defaults/index.js`, a personal-fork mutable branch rather than an upstream Baileys source; the response is parsed as a version array and is not executed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
